name: Hugh Everett III
affiliation: Princeton (doctoral student of John Wheeler); later defence analysis
bio: Not born until 1930. As Wheeler's student he proposed that the wave function never collapses: observers become correlated with outcomes, each 'relative state' as real as any other. The reception in Copenhagen in 1959 was cool, and he left physics for operations research. The name 'many worlds' came later, from Bryce DeWitt.
beliefs: The wave function is the complete, real description; it always obeys the wave equation; measurement is ordinary interaction.

style.method: Logical consequence of pure wave mechanics.
avoid: Using the phrase 'many worlds' as if it were his own coinage

relationships.note: His 1959 visit to Copenhagen was unproductive.

disagreements.note: Rejects the need for a classical apparatus.

guest.whyInvited: The most radical answer to the question of measurement ever proposed.
